messages:
maya: Observed weird cancellations when the SDK retries on connection reset — a bunch of in-flight requests get CancelledError and the AsyncClient session appears to close mid-flight.

jonathan: Ugh. Which transport/version? httpx AsyncClient + httpcore? Any stacktrace?

maya: Yep httpx 0.23.3 + httpcore. Repro is small: create several tasks that call the SDK async client concurrently, then kill the TCP connection on the server. Most tasks come back as CancelledError.

maya: Minimal repro snippet:```
async with SDKAsyncClient() as c:
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(c.generate(i)) for i in range(8)]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
```
When the server drops the socket we immediately call our reconnect logic which recreates the client and we see a bunch of CancelledError in results.

li: That sounds like we're doing `await self._client.aclose()` in the reconnect path. Closing the httpx client will cancel underlying tasks. We should avoid that while requests are in-flight.

maya: Right — we close to flush bad connections but doing that unconditionally is causing the cancels. Shielding with `asyncio.shield` helped in my quick test.

sam: Shield is a stopgap. Also if we never close the old client we might leak sockets. We need a graceful drain: stop accepting new requests, wait for in-flight counter to go to zero (with timeout), then close.

jonathan: Agreed. Another angle: our retry policy currently triggers immediate client recreation on any ConnectionError/ReadError. Can we adjust to mark the client unhealthy and only recreate after a short backoff? That would reduce churn.

maya: I dug into logs, snippet of the error chain:```
httpx._exceptions.ReadError: EOF occurred in violation of protocol (_ssl.c:1053)
CancelledError
```
The CancelledError originates right after `aclose()` is awaited during reconnect.

li: Proposed fix: add an in-flight request counter on the SDK client, increment at request start, decrement at exit (finally). On reconnect path: set `draining=True`, wait for counter==0 or timeout, then close. Also don't call `aclose()` synchronously from a request failure handler.

maya: I'll write a failing unit test that reproduces behavior under artificial socket drop. Using pytest-asyncio + pytest-timeout should work. Test path: tests/async/test_reconnect_cancel.py.

infra-bot: CI: re-run requested by maya — macOS runner flaky :retry: (automated)

sam: Also note: our stub for AsyncClient.close() in typeshed is missing `async` marker in SDK typings, people keep calling it synchronously in examples which complicates reasoning. Filing a typing issue in the SDK repo.

jonathan: Good catch on the typings. Once li has a draft we should run integration that simulates intermittent resets (tcpkill or iptables) to ensure no task cancellations and no leaked file descriptors.

li: I'll prototype the in-flight counter + drain tonight, push a draft branch with tests. ETA EOD tomorrow for a PR.

maya: Thanks. If anyone can try the branch earlier and run their load tests that would be great — especially dogfood on our long-poll workload.

sam: One more idea — consider using `client.aclose()` in a background task and shield active requests from cancellation; but that still requires careful lifecycle handling. Drain+timeout seems cleaner.

maya: Agreed. I'll add a short design note in the PR describing the drain lifecycle and backoff tuning.

jonathan: After fix let's add an e2e script in infra/tools/e2e that flips the server connection and asserts all requests either succeed or return a retryable error (no CancelledError).

maya: Acknowledged — will follow up in PR comments.
